source_refs.note: Topic 8.6, printed page 172, with Quick Check 8.3 (b) as the self-check.

items: At chemical equilibrium the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.
The state of equilibrium in a reversible reaction can be approached from either side, starting with reactants or with products.
A catalyst does not change the equilibrium position or the equilibrium constant; it helps to attain equilibrium earlier.
The value of the equilibrium constant does not depend on the initial concentrations of the reactants; it is constant and depends on temperature only.

blocks.title: Keep in mind
blocks.text: If pure solids or pure liquids take part in an equilibrium, their concentrations are not included in the equilibrium constant expression, because a change in the amount of a pure solid or liquid has no effect on the equilibrium constant.

blocks.prompt: Why do the forward reaction rates slow down as a reversible reaction approaches equilibrium?
blocks.explanation: The forward rate depends on the concentrations of the reactants, which fall as they are converted into products, so fewer reactant collisions occur each second. Meanwhile the growing products make the reverse rate rise, until the two rates meet at equilibrium.

items: At equilibrium concentrations are constant; it can be reached from either side; a catalyst only hastens it; the equilibrium constant depends on temperature alone, not on starting amounts; pure solids and liquids are omitted from the expression.
